overview: This 429-page file documents Japanese international shortwave broadcasting in 1941 through translated transcripts, program guides, monitoring reports, and U.S. diplomatic and FBI correspondence. Broadcasts promote Japan’s war in China and expansion into French Indochina, respond to economic sanctions and Allied diplomacy, and address overseas audiences as relations with the United States deteriorate.
interest: Transcripts and monitoring reports reveal how Japan tailored wartime messages abroad, alongside U.S. assessments and evidence of reception failures.
